novelty_flags.label: Project-level published survey
novelty_flags.one_line: The review omits Lin, Gao, Blanchet, and Glynn (ICML 2025), a close causal-OT partial-identification and convergence comparator; add it and state why its covariate-assisted binary setting is orthogonal to the unconditional growing-K frontier.

soundness_flags.label: Proposition 5
soundness_flags.one_line: With P2=(-Id)#nu and all remaining margins delta0, the claim is exactly the definitions of L and W2 after substitution, so it is a vacuous proposition rather than a research target.

soundness_flags.label: Proposition 11 / def:star-transformation
soundness_flags.one_line: The core supplies neither a finite declared outcome bound ensuring bY<infinity nor a superpopulation/iid law linking the selected STAR Y(k) values to the Pk product experiment, so the scaled endpoint and sampling guarantee are not defined on the stated model.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 724-725, Theorem 1 equation (6) and Proposition 2; p. 727, Section 4.3.1
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 1 gives n^{-1/2}+min{K^{-1},K^{-1/2}(n/K)^{-2/d}} for d>4 and Proposition 2 gives the printed high-dimensional lower expression; the STAR application uses cells 161, 37, and 36.
The published article concerns plug-in empirical OT with smooth costs, n^{-2/d} high-dimensional behavior, and minimax lower bounds for the two-margin problem.

The paper supplies uniformly valid randomized-experiment inference based on OT duality even with inaccurate initial conditional-distribution estimates; it does not state an all-arm minimax expected-excess-length converse.

The paper studies causal partial-identification bounds through covariate-aware OT, supplies an estimator and convergence analysis, and is a close but non-subsuming comparator because it targets conditional/covariate-assisted OT rather than the proposed unconditional growing-K frontier.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add Lin--Gao--Blanchet--Glynn (ICML 2025) and its later covariate-assisted estimation follow-up to related work, explicitly separating conditional binary COT from the arbitrary-margin unconditional all-K problem.

Replace the STAR scale by a declared finite known bound and add a precise superpopulation assignment-and-subsampling law that identifies the selected observations with independent draws from the three transformed marginals.
Move the two-margin identity to a sanity-reduction/helper, then use the recovered proposition slot for a nontrivial generic-class rematching obstruction or an explicit all-arm lower-bound family.

For the exact-frontier OEQ, specify a finite-support simultaneous-marginal perturbation family and its observable separation target, so a future lower-bound proof has a concrete rematching-resistant construction benchmark.

recommended_next_step: Revise the STAR sampling/scale contract, demote Proposition 5 to a sanity reduction, and update the published comparison set before advancing the all-K frontier angle.
